Dutch health authorities issued an urgent warning after test centres in the Netherlands identified a batch of ecstasy pills shaped like US President Donald Trump containing a potentially fatal toxic chemical.
The Utrecht-based Trimbos Institute raised the alarm following the discovery of para-methoxymethamfetamine (PMMA) in several submitted samples. The tablets, stamped with Trump's likeness on one side and "NL" on the reverse, have appeared in bright yellow and green shades across national nightlife circuits.
Toxic Imposter Poses Severe Overdose Risk
PMMA shares chemical similarities with MDMA—the active component in standard ecstasy—but behaves dangerously in the body. Unlike typical stimulants, PMMA takes significantly longer to kick in and fails to produce the expected euphoric high.
This delayed onset often tricks users into taking additional doses, leading to accidental poisoning. Physical reactions range from violent nausea and rapid heart rates to severe heatstroke, seizures, organ failure, and sudden cardiac arrest.
Global Travellers on High Alert
While Dutch officials confirm no fatalities have been recorded from this specific batch yet, medical experts warn international travellers and students to exercise extreme caution.
Trimbos spokesperson Anniek Groothuis stated that they did not know of any victims where PMMA had been found in their blood yet.. Even so, public health monitors continue pushing notifications across nightlife networks to prevent casualties.
Persistent Counterfeiting in Western European Markets
The Netherlands remains a primary production hub for synthetic narcotics despite strict enforcement laws. Official statistics show over half a million Dutch residents consumed ecstasy in recent years, maintaining a lucrative market for illicit laboratories.
Novelty branding remains a common marketing tactic among illicit drug manufacturers targeting young festival-goers. German police previously intercepted thousands of orange Trump-shaped tablets in 2017, which were trafficked with political slogans. Dutch testing facilities now scan all major nightlife hubs as public health teams work to clear the current batch from circulation.
